messages:
acme_engineer: Hi, hitting a weird billing/5xx issue on streaming responses. Our editor extension shows the stream cut mid-response and we got charged & counted as a 5xx. Can we get help reproducing and clarifying why this is billed?

maya: Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal repro and a sample request_id? Also which SDK / HTTP client are you using (node, fetch, curl)?

acme_engineer: Using our VSCode extension which uses node-fetch under the hood. Sample request id: req_2024-07-28_7a9c2f. Quick log snippet from the client: ``ERROR: fetch failed: write EPIPE``

aj: Thanks. Two quick things: 1) do you have a server-side trace or gateway trace ID? 2) does the client close the socket abruptly (user cancels) or just stops reading?

acme_engineer: The user hits ESC in the editor which cancels the read stream. Client logs: ``Client stream aborted by user; socket FIN seen locally``. On our side it looks like Redwood reported a 502 and it was flagged as a server 5xx in billing.

eli: @aj tagging SRE here — this sounds like an EOF detection mismatch between the proxy and the backend. If the proxy interprets the downstream FIN as a mid-request failure it can surface a 5xx. @sre-bot can you pull gateway logs for req_2024-07-28_7a9c2f?

sre-bot: logs attached (excerpt): ``[gateway] 2024-07-28T15:04:12Z req_7a9c2f upstream=TOKENGW backend=runtime-gpu-03 status=502 note="upstream_read: connection reset by peer" conn_state=FIN_RCVD``

maya: That note looks like the proxy saw a reset from the backend while the client had already closed the read. Could be a TCP RST race. Do you have a pcap or tcpdump?

acme_engineer: No pcap, but here's a short repro we used in node. It's basically: ``const r = await fetch(url); const reader = r.body.getReader(); // user cancels -> controller.abort();`` Users cancel at random points and we see the same.

eli: Can you try a curl repro? curl behaves more predictably for streaming. Example we asked them to run:``
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-1" 
# then ctrl-c during the stream
``

acme_engineer: Ran that — got a local "Broken pipe" and on the gateway side: ``runtime: downstream EOF before body complete -> 502``

aj: OK, two concurrent problems here: 1) stream termination is being classified as an upstream error in some code paths, 2) billing classification treats 502 from runtime as billable 5xx. We should not bill customers for client-initiated cancels.

dev-xavier: I dug into the runtime handler. There's a heuristic: if backend returns read error while sending chunks we map to 5xx. But we don't always correlate the downstream socket state. Need to add logic to prefer client-side FIN/RST indication when present.

maya: Action items I propose:
- SRE: correlate connection-level flags (FIN vs RST) across proxy/runtime for that request id and attach to ticket.
- Billing: exclude token charges when request appears client-aborted within N seconds of gateway EOF.
- Eng-runtime: adjust EOF/abort heuristic to not classify as a 5xx if downstream closed the read first.
- Support: send repro steps to customer and validate non-billing path after changes.

billing-bot: Created billing ticket BL-9831 referencing req_2024-07-28_7a9c2f. Status: triage.

sre-bot: Added gateway tcp flags to BL-9831. Excerpt: ``tcp: client FIN -> proxy FIN_RCVD -> backend attempt write -> backend RST observed``

eli: That pattern matches the classic "half-close write after FIN then RST" race. Runtime tries to stream tokens after client FIN -> kernel returns EPIPE -> runtime logs upstream_read error and proxy maps to 502.

acme_engineer: So are we expecting a config change only or a code fix? We need a timeline because this affects customer invoices.

dev-xavier: Short term: SRE can add a filter that marks requests with client FIN within 2s of error as client-abort (non-5xx) in billing aggregator. That is a config/metric change we can ship this week. Medium term: runtime patch to interrogate socket state before escalating to 5xx — PR target next sprint.

maya: For the customer: can you run the curl repro and include the exact HTTP response headers you receive (we need the gateway timestamp header x-rw-gateway-ts) so we can fully reconcile the billing window? Also please tell us the approximate time they hit ESC so we can match tcp flags.

acme_engineer: Will run now and attach headers + exact wall time. One more question: is there any recommended client-side pattern to avoid this?

eli: Two recommendations: 1) send a short keepalive / heartbeat on long streams (we add a noop token every 30s) so intermediate proxies don't assume silence; 2) when aborting, try a graceful close on the application level (send application-level cancel message) before shutdown if possible. Both reduce races.

acme_engineer: Helpful — implementing an app-level cancel is doable.

maya: Logging follow-ups: I'll open a support incident (SUP-4812) to track customer impact, attach BL-9831 and the runtime ticket, and we'll update you when SRE posts the TCP dump.

sre-bot: Incident SUP-4812 created. ETA for billing interim filter: 3 business days. ETA for runtime heuristic patch: ~2 weeks (engineering sprint schedule).

aj: For traceability, add a metric that counts "stream-client-abort-flagged" vs "stream-5xx-classified" so we can watch regression.

dev-xavier: Will add metric and dashboard. Also adding a unit test that simulates downstream FIN followed by backend EPIPE to ensure we don't flip to 5xx in new code.

acme_engineer: Thanks everyone. I'll run the curl repro and post headers and wallclock time in this thread. We appreciate the timely triage. :pray:

maya: Thanks. We'll follow up in this thread once the billing filter is in place and when runtime PR merges. :thumbsup:
